question: What is the minimum experience required for a building official in Florida?
answer: A building official must have at least 10 years' experience as an architect, engineer, inspector, contractor or superintendent of construction, with at least 5 years in a supervisory capacity.
ground_truth:
A101.1 Building official.

The building official shall have at least 10 years' experience or equivalent as an architect, engineer, inspector, contractor or superintendent of construction, or any combination of these, 5 years of which shall have been supervisory experience.

question: Are single-wall metal pipe connectors permitted to pass through walls, floors or ceilings?
answer: No, single-wall metal pipe connectors are not permitted to pass through any wall, floor or ceiling except as permitted by specific code provisions.
ground_truth:
G2427.10.14 (503.10.14) Passage through ceilings, floors or walls.

Single-wall metal pipe connectors shall not pass through any wall, floor or ceiling except as permitted by Section G2427.7.4.

question: What is the minimum net glazed area required for natural light in an occupied space?
answer: The minimum net glazed area must be at least 8 percent of the floor area of the room being served.
ground_truth:
1205.2 Natural light.

The minimum net glazed area shall be not less than 8 percent of the floor area of the room served.

question: When is mechanical ventilation required for bathrooms in residential construction?
answer: Bathrooms must be mechanically ventilated in accordance with the Florida Building Code, Mechanical.
ground_truth:
1203.5.2.1 Bathrooms.

Rooms containing bathtubs, showers, spas and similar bathing fixtures shall be mechanically ventilated in accordance with the Florida Building Code, Mechanical.

question: What is the required minimum width for strip underlayment at floor deck joints?
answer: The minimum width is 3 3/4 inches for self-adhering polymer-modified bitumen membrane or self-adhering flexible flashing tape, applied over all joints in the roof decking.
ground_truth:
1507.1.1.1
A minimum 33/4-inch-wide (95 mm) strip of selfadhering polymer-modified bitumen membrane complying with ASTM D1970 or self-adhering flexible flashing tape complying with AAMA 711, Level 3 [for exposure up to 176°F (80°C)], installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions for the deck material, shall be applied over all joints in the roof decking.

question: How many fasteners are required per strip shingle for asphalt shingles?
answer: Asphalt shingles must be secured with not less than four fasteners per strip shingle or two fasteners per individual shingle.
ground_truth:
1507.2.7 Attachment.

Asphalt shingles shall have the minimum number of fasteners required by the manufacturer and Section 1504.1. Asphalt shingles shall be secured to the roof with not less than four fasteners per strip shingle or two fasteners per individual shingle.

question: What is the maximum horizontal length permitted for a single-wall vent connector?
answer: The maximum horizontal length of a single-wall connector is 75 percent of the height of the chimney or vent, except for engineered systems.
ground_truth:
G2427.10.9 (503.10.9) Length of vent connector.

The maximum horizontal length of a single-wall connector shall be 75 percent of the height of the chimney or vent except for engineered systems.

question: What is the minimum slope required for a vent connector?
answer: A vent connector must slope upward toward the vent or chimney at not less than 1/4 inch per foot.
ground_truth:
G2427.10.8 (503.10.8) Slope.

A vent connector shall be installed without dips or sags and shall slope upward toward the vent or chimney not less than 1/4 inch per foot (21 mm/m).

question: What minimum clearance is required between a draft hood relief opening and adjacent surfaces?
answer: A draft hood relief opening must be at least 6 inches from any surface except the appliance or venting system it serves.
ground_truth:
G2427.12.7 (503.12.7) Clearance.

A draft hood shall be located so its relief opening is not less than 6 inches (152 mm) from any surface except that of the appliance it serves and the venting system to which the draft hood is connected.

question: What is the minimum size for water service pipe in Florida?
answer: The minimum size water service pipe is 3/4 inch.
ground_truth:
AP201.1 Size of water-service mains, branch mains and risers.

The minimum size water service pipe shall be 3/4 inch (19.1 mm).

question: How many exits are required for an occupant load of 600 persons on a single story?
answer: For an occupant load of 501 to 1,000 persons, three separate exits or access to exits are required from the story.
ground_truth:
TABLE 1006.3.2

MINIMUM NUMBER OF EXITS OR ACCESS TO EXITS PER STORY

OCCUPANT LOAD PER STORY: 501-1,000
MINIMUM NUMBER OF EXITS OR ACCESS TO EXITS FROM STORY: 3

question: What is the minimum illumination level required for means of egress?
answer: The means of egress illumination level must be not less than 1 footcandle at the walking surface.
ground_truth:
1008.2.1 Illumination level under normal power.

The means of egress illumination level shall be not less than 1 footcandle (11 lux) at the walking surface.

question: What minimum illumination is required along exit access stairways when in use?
answer: Exit access stairways require illumination of not less than 10 footcandles at the walking surface when the stairway is in use.
ground_truth:
1008.2.1 Illumination level under normal power.

Along exit access stairways, exit stairways and at their required landings, the illumination level shall not be less than 10 footcandles at the walking surface when the stairway is in use.

question: What standards govern exit door placement in electrical rooms?
answer: Exit or exit access doors in electrical rooms must comply with NFPA 70 Section 110.26 for equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 for equipment rated over 1,000 volts.
ground_truth:
1006.2.2.4 Electrical rooms.

The location and number of exit or exit access doorways shall be provided for electrical rooms in accordance with Section 110.26 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated 1,000 volts or less, and Section 110.33 of NFPA 70 for electrical equipment rated over 1,000 volts.

question: What is the maximum permitted clearance between a door and its jambs and sills?
answer: The maximum clearance between any door, door jambs and sills is 3/8 inch.
ground_truth:
F101.4 Doors.

Doors on which metal protection has been applied shall be hinged so as to be free swinging. When closed, the maximum clearance between any door, door jambs and sills shall be not greater than 3/8 inch (9.5 mm).

question: What size mesh or screening is required for foundation wall ventilation openings to prevent rodent entry?
answer: Openings must be covered with perforated sheet metal, expanded sheet metal, cast-iron grills, extruded aluminum vents, or hardware cloth with openings not exceeding 1/4 inch.
ground_truth:
F101.2 Foundation wall ventilation openings.

Foundation wall ventilation openings shall be covered for their height and width with perforated sheet metal plates no less than 0.070 inch (1.8 mm) thick, expanded sheet metal plates not less than 0.047 inch (1.2 mm) thick, cast-iron grills or grating, extruded aluminum load-bearing vents or with hardware cloth of 0.035 inch (0.89 mm) wire or heavier. The openings therein shall not exceed 1/4 inch (6.4 mm).

question: What fire code requirements apply to permanently installed artificial decorative vegetation near buildings?
answer: Artificial decorative vegetation exceeding 6 feet in height and permanently installed within 5 feet of a building, or on the roof, must comply with the Florida Fire Prevention Code.
ground_truth:
419.1 Artificial decorative vegetation.

Artificial decorative vegetation exceeding 6 feet (1830 mm) in height and permanently installed outdoors within 5 feet (1524 mm) of a building, or on the roof of a building, shall comply with the Florida Fire Prevention Code.

question: What fire-resistance rating is required for the enclosure of spray rooms?
answer: Spray rooms must be enclosed with not less than 1-hour fire barriers or horizontal assemblies, or both.
ground_truth:
[F] 416.2 Spray rooms.

Spray rooms shall be enclosed with not less than 1-hour fire barriers constructed in accordance with Section 707 or horizontal assemblies constructed in accordance with Section 711, or both.

question: What materials are prohibited for interior surfaces of spray rooms?
answer: Aluminum is prohibited for the interior surfaces of spray rooms.
ground_truth:
[F] 416.2.1 Surfaces.

The interior surfaces of spray rooms shall be smooth and shall be so constructed to permit the free passage of exhaust air from all parts of the interior and to facilitate washing and cleaning, and shall be so designed to confine residues within the room. Aluminum shall not be used.

question: What is the minimum clearance required between overhead heating pipes and combustible contents in a drying room?
answer: Overhead heating pipes must maintain a clearance of not less than 2 inches from combustible contents in the dryer.
ground_truth:
[F] 417.2 Piping clearance.

Overhead heating pipes shall have a clearance of not less than 2 inches (51 mm) from combustible contents in the dryer.

question: When must metal enclosures in drying rooms be insulated from combustible materials?
answer: When the operating temperature is 175°F or more, metal enclosures must be insulated by not less than 12 inches of airspace or lined with 1/4-inch insulating mill board or equivalent.
ground_truth:
[F] 417.3 Insulation.

Where the operating temperature of the dryer is 175°F (79°C) or more, metal enclosures shall be insulated from adjacent combustible materials by not less than 12 inches (305 mm) of airspace, or the metal walls shall be lined with 1/4-inch (6.4 mm) insulating mill board or other approved equivalent insulation.

question: Are hydrogen fuel gas rooms permitted to be located below grade?
answer: No, hydrogen fuel gas rooms must not be located below grade.
ground_truth:
[F] 421.3 Location.

Hydrogen fuel gas rooms shall not be located below grade.

question: What pressure relationship must a hydrogen fuel gas room maintain relative to surrounding spaces?
answer: Hydrogen fuel gas rooms must be maintained at a negative pressure relative to surrounding rooms and spaces.
ground_truth:
[F] 421.4.1 Pressure control.

Hydrogen fuel gas rooms shall be provided with a ventilation system designed to maintain the room at a negative pressure in relation to surrounding rooms and spaces.

question: What automatic actions must occur when a gas detection alarm is triggered in a hydrogen fuel gas room?
answer: Gas detection alarm activation must trigger both distinct audible and visible alarm signals inside and outside the room, and automatic activation of the mechanical exhaust ventilation system.
ground_truth:
[F] 421.6.1 System activation.

Activation of a gas detection alarm shall result in both of the following:

1. Initiation of distinct audible and visible alarm signals both inside and outside of the hydrogen fuel gas room.

2. Automatic activation of the mechanical exhaust ventilation system.

question: What is the minimum length for solid wall segments in residential concrete construction?
answer: Only solid wall segments equal to or greater than 24 inches in length may be counted toward the required total length of solid wall.
ground_truth:
R608.7.2.1 Minimum length of solid wall segment and maximum spacing.

Only solid wall segments equal to or greater than 24 inches (610 mm) in length shall be included in the total length of solid wall required by Section R608.7.1.

question: What is the maximum clear opening width permitted in residential concrete construction walls?
answer: The maximum clear opening width is 18 feet.
ground_truth:
R608.7.2.1 Minimum length of solid wall segment and maximum spacing.

The maximum clear opening width shall be 18 feet (5486 mm).

question: What is the minimum development length for reinforcing bars in concrete masonry?
answer: The minimum development length is the greater of 12 inches or 40 bar diameters, and need not exceed 72 bar diameters.
ground_truth:
2107.6 TMS 402, Section 6.1.5.1.1 Development of bar reinforcement in tension or compression.

The required development length of reinforcing bars shall be determined by Equation (6-1), but shall not be less than 12 inches (305 mm) or 40 db and need not be greater than 72 db.

question: What types of masonry units are covered by the Florida Building Code?
answer: Concrete masonry units, clay or shale masonry units, stone masonry units, glass unit masonry, and AAC masonry units are all covered.
ground_truth:
2103.1 Masonry units.

Concrete masonry units, clay or shale masonry units, stone masonry units, glass unit masonry and AAC masonry units shall comply with Article 2.3 of TMS 602.

question: Can second-hand masonry units be reused without any preparation?
answer: No. Second-hand units must be cleaned of old mortar and must be whole and sound, free from cracks or defects that would interfere with proper laying or use.
ground_truth:
2103.1.1 Second-hand units.

Second-hand masonry units shall not be reused unless they conform to the requirements of new units. The units shall be of whole, sound materials and free from cracks and other defects that will interfere with proper laying or use. Old mortar shall be cleaned from the unit before reuse.

question: Is masonry permitted to be supported on wood girders?
answer: No, masonry shall not be supported on wood girders or other wood construction except as permitted in Section 2304.13.
ground_truth:
2104.1.1 Support on wood.

Masonry shall not be supported on wood girders or other forms of wood construction except as permitted in Section 2304.13.

question: Where must the center of gravity lie for projecting masonry cornices without structural anchorage?
answer: Unless structural support and anchorage are provided, the center of gravity of projecting masonry or molded cornices must lie within the middle one-third of the supporting wall.
ground_truth:
2104.1.2 Molded cornices.

Unless structural support and anchorage are provided to resist the overturning moment, the center of gravity of projecting masonry or molded cornices shall lie within the middle one-third of the supporting wall.

question: What minimum thickness is required for a masonry foundation apron?
answer: Where constructed of masonry or concrete materials, the apron must be not less than 4 inches in thickness.
ground_truth:
F101.6.1.1 Apron.

Where constructed of masonry or concrete materials, the apron shall be not less than 4 inches (102 mm) in thickness.

question: What is the required net free ventilating area ratio for attic spaces?
answer: The net free ventilating area must be not less than 1/150 of the area of the space ventilated.
ground_truth:
1203.2 Ventilation required.

The net free ventilating area shall be not less than 1/150 of the area of the space ventilated.

question: Under what conditions can the required attic ventilation area be reduced to 1/300?
answer: The area may be reduced to 1/300 when at least 40 percent and not more than 50 percent of the required ventilation is provided by upper ventilators located not more than 3 feet below the ridge, with the balance provided by eave or cornice vents.
ground_truth:
1203.2 Ventilation required.

Exception: The net free cross-ventilation area shall be permitted to be reduced to 1/300 provided at least 40 percent and not more than 50 percent of the required venting area is provided by ventilators located in the upper portion of the attic or rafter space. Upper ventilators shall be located not more than 3 feet (914 mm) below the ridge or highest point of the space, measured vertically, with the balance of the ventilation provided by eave or cornice vents.

question: What opening dimensions are required for attic ventilation openings to exclude birds and rodents?
answer: Openings for ventilation must have a least dimension of not less than 1/16 inch and not more than 1/4 inch.
ground_truth:
1203.2.1 Openings into attic.

Exterior openings into the attic space of any building intended for human occupancy shall be protected to prevent the entry of birds, squirrels, rodents, snakes and other similar creatures. Openings for ventilation having a least dimension of not less than 1/16 inch (1.6 mm) and not more than 1/4 inch (6.4 mm) shall be permitted.

question: What minimum indoor temperature must heating systems maintain in occupied spaces?
answer: Heating systems must maintain an indoor temperature of not less than 68°F at a point 3 feet above the floor on the design heating day.
ground_truth:
1204.1 Equipment and systems.

Interior spaces intended for human occupancy shall be provided with active or passive space heating systems capable of maintaining an indoor temperature of not less than 68°F (20°C) at a point 3 feet (914 mm) above the floor on the design heating day.

question: What is the minimum average illumination level required for artificial lighting in an occupied room?
answer: Artificial light must provide an average illumination of 10 footcandles over the area of the room at a height of 30 inches above floor level.
ground_truth:
1205.3 Artificial light.

Artificial light shall be provided that is adequate to provide an average illumination of 10 footcandles (107 lux) over the area of the room at a height of 30 inches (762 mm) above the floor level.

question: What illumination level is required on stairway treads in dwelling units?
answer: Stairways within dwelling units must have illumination on tread runs of not less than 1 footcandle.
ground_truth:
1205.4 Stairway illumination.

Stairways within dwelling units and exterior stairways serving a dwelling unit shall have an illumination level on tread runs of not less than 1 footcandle (11 lux).

question: What is the minimum required duration for emergency lighting in means of egress?
answer: The emergency power system must provide power for not less than 90 minutes.
ground_truth:
1008.3.4 Duration.

The emergency power system shall provide power for a duration of not less than 90 minutes and shall consist of storage batteries, unit equipment or an on-site generator.

question: What illumination levels are required under emergency power along egress paths?
answer: Emergency lighting must provide an initial average of not less than 1 footcandle and a minimum at any point of 0.1 footcandle measured along the path of egress at floor level.
ground_truth:
1008.3.5 Illumination level under emergency power.

Emergency lighting facilities shall be arranged to provide initial illumination that is not less than an average of 1 footcandle (11 lux) and a minimum at any point of 0.1 footcandle (1 lux) measured along the path of egress at floor level.

question: What is the minimum separation distance required between two exits or exit access doorways?
answer: They must be placed a distance apart equal to not less than one-half of the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the building or area being served.
ground_truth:
1007.1.1 Two exits or exit access doorways.

Where two exits, exit access doorways, exit access stairways or ramps, or any combination thereof, are required from any portion of the exit access, they shall be placed a distance apart equal to not less than one-half of the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the building or area to be served measured in a straight line between them.

question: How is the required exit separation distance affected when a building has a full automatic sprinkler system?
answer: In buildings equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system per Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2, the separation distance may be reduced to not less than one-third of the maximum overall diagonal dimension.
ground_truth:
1007.1.1 Two exits or exit access doorways.

Exceptions:

2. Where a building is equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2, the separation distance shall be not less than one-third of the length of the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the area served.

question: When is a single exit permitted from a story?
answer: A single exit is permitted where the occupant load, number of dwelling units, and common path of egress travel distance do not exceed the values in Table 1006.3.3(1) or 1006.3.3(2).
ground_truth:
1006.3.3 Single exits.

A single exit or access to a single exit shall be permitted from any story or occupied roof where one of the following conditions exists:

1. The occupant load, number of dwelling units and common path of egress travel distance do not exceed the values in Table 1006.3.3(1) or 1006.3.3(2).

question: What fire-resistance construction is required for walls separating dwelling units in Group R occupancies?
answer: Walls separating dwelling units in the same building must be constructed as fire partitions in accordance with Section 708.
ground_truth:
420.2 Separation walls.

Walls separating dwelling units in the same building, walls separating sleeping units in the same building and walls separating dwelling or sleeping units from other occupancies contiguous to them in the same building shall be constructed as fire partitions in accordance with Section 708.

question: What construction type is required for floor assemblies separating dwelling units?
answer: Floor assemblies separating dwelling units or sleeping units in the same building must be constructed as horizontal assemblies in accordance with Section 711.
ground_truth:
420.3 Horizontal separation.

Floor assemblies separating dwelling units in the same buildings, floor assemblies separating sleeping units in the same building and floor assemblies separating dwelling or sleeping units from other occupancies contiguous to them in the same building shall be constructed as horizontal assemblies in accordance with Section 711.

question: What is the maximum permitted smoke compartment area in Group I-1 Condition 2 occupancies?
answer: Smoke compartments must not exceed 22,500 square feet in area.
ground_truth:
420.4 Smoke barriers in Group I-1, Condition 2.

Smoke barriers shall be provided in Group I-1, Condition 2, to subdivide every story used by persons receiving care, treatment or sleeping and to provide other stories with an occupant load of 50 or more persons, into no fewer than two smoke compartments. Such stories shall be divided into smoke compartments with an area of not more than 22,500 square feet (2092 m2).

question: What is the maximum travel distance from any point in a Group I-1 smoke compartment to a smoke barrier door?
answer: The distance of travel from any point in a smoke compartment to a smoke barrier door must not exceed 200 feet.
ground_truth:
420.4 Smoke barriers in Group I-1, Condition 2.

The distance of travel from any point in a smoke compartment to a smoke barrier door shall not exceed 200 feet (60 960 mm).

question: What minimum refuge area per care recipient is required in Group I-1 facilities?
answer: The refuge area must provide not less than 15 net square feet for each care recipient.
ground_truth:
420.4.1 Refuge area.

The size of the refuge area shall provide the following:

1. Not less than 15 net square feet (1.4 m2) for each care recipient.

question: What is the minimum openable area required for natural ventilation of a space?
answer: The openable area of openings to the outdoors must be not less than 4 percent of the floor area being ventilated.
ground_truth:
1203.5.1 Ventilation area required.

The openable area of the openings to the outdoors shall be not less than 4 percent of the floor area being ventilated.

question: What minimum opening size is required to naturally ventilate an interior room through an adjoining space?
answer: The opening to the adjoining room must be not less than 8 percent of the floor area of the interior room, but not less than 25 square feet.
ground_truth:
1203.5.1.1 Adjoining spaces.

Where rooms and spaces without openings to the outdoors are ventilated through an adjoining room, the opening to the adjoining room shall be unobstructed and shall have an area of not less than 8 percent of the floor area of the interior room or space, but not less than 25 square feet (2.3 m2).

question: What is the minimum thickness of a sub-slab or soil-cover membrane required in passive radon-resistant construction?
answer: The membrane shall consist of a minimum 0.006 inch (6 mil) thick single layer of polyethylene or equivalent nondeteriorating nonporous material with a permeance of less than 0.3 perm.
ground_truth: Section B302.1: A sub-slab or soil-cover membrane shall consist of a minimum 0.006 inch (0.152 mm) (6 mil) thick single layer of polyethylene. Polyvinylchloride (PVC), ethylene propylene diene terpolymer (EPDM), neoprene or other nondeteriorating nonporous material may be used instead of polyethylene, provided the installed thickness has greater or equal resistance to air flow, puncturing, cutting and tearing, and a permeance of less than 0.3 perm as determined in accordance with ASTM E96.

question: What is required for sealing penetrations in soil membranes during passive radon-resistant construction?
answer: At all points where pipes, conduits, stakes, or other objects pass through the membrane, the membrane shall be fitted to within 1/2 inch of the penetration and sealed with either mastic or tape.
ground_truth: Section B302.7: At all points where pipes, conduits, stakes, reinforcing bars or other objects pass through the membrane, the membrane shall be fitted to within 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) of the penetration and sealed to the penetration.

question: What work does not require a permit for electrical installations in accordance with Appendix K?
answer: Listed cord-and plug-connected temporary decorative lighting, reinstallation of attachment plug receptacles, replacement of branch circuit overcurrent devices of the required capacity in the same location, and electrical equipment operating at less than 25 volts and not capable of supplying more than 50 watts are exempt from permit requirements.
ground_truth: Section K103.2 Work exempt from permit: The following work shall be exempt from the requirement for a permit: 1. Listed cord- and plug-connected temporary decorative lighting. 2. Reinstallation of attachment plug receptacles. 3. Replacement of branch circuit overcurrent devices of the required capacity in the same location.

question: What is the purpose of electrical code provisions in Appendix K?
answer: A purpose of this code is to establish minimum requirements to safeguard public health, safety and general welfare by regulating and controlling the design, construction, installation, quality of materials, location, operation and maintenance or use of electrical systems and equipment.
ground_truth: Section K101.1: A purpose of this code is to establish minimum requirements to safeguard public health, safety and general welfare by regulating and controlling the design, construction, installation, quality of materials, location, operation and maintenance or use of electrical systems and equipment.

question: What is the minimum slope required for built-up roofs to allow for proper drainage?
answer: Built-up roofs shall have a design slope of not less than one-fourth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2-percent slope) for drainage, except for coal-tar built-up roofs that shall have a design slope of not less than one-eighth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (1-percent slope).
ground_truth: Section 1507.10.1: Built-up roofs shall have a design slope of not less than one-fourth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2-percent slope) for drainage, except for coal-tar built-up roofs that shall have a design slope of not less than one-eighth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (1-percent slope).

question: What is the minimum roof slope required for asphalt shingles?
answer: Asphalt shingles shall only be used on roof slopes of two units vertical in 12 units horizontal (17-percent slope) or greater.
ground_truth: Section 1507.2.2: Asphalt shingles shall only be used on roof slopes of two units vertical in 12 units horizontal (17- percent slope) or greater.

question: What fire classification must roof assemblies in Type IIA construction buildings meet?
answer: Buildings of Type IIA construction shall have roof assemblies classified as Class B per Table 1505.1.
ground_truth: TABLE 1505.1 MINIMUM ROOF ASSEMBLY CLASSIFICATION FOR TYPES OF CONSTRUCTION: Type IIA buildings require Class B roof assemblies.

question: What is the minimum thickness required for metal flashing material in roof assemblies?
answer: Metal flashing materials must meet the minimum thicknesses specified in Table 1503.2, including copper at 1 ounce per square foot and aluminum at 0.024 inch.
ground_truth: TABLE 1503.2 METAL FLASHING MATERIAL: Lists minimum thicknesses for copper (1 oz), aluminum (0.024 in), and other materials.

question: Where must flashing be installed in roof assemblies according to Section 1503.2?
answer: Flashing shall be installed at wall and roof intersections, at gutters, wherever there is a change in roof slope or direction and around roof openings.
ground_truth: Section 1503.2.1 Locations: Flashing shall be installed at wall and roof intersections, at gutters, wherever there is a change in roof slope or direction and around roof openings.

question: What is the minimum fastener penetration required for asphalt shingle fasteners into roof sheathing?
answer: Fasteners must penetrate through the roofing materials and a minimum of 3/4 inch into the roof sheathing, or through the sheathing if it is less than 3/4 inch thick.
ground_truth: Section 1507.2.6: Fasteners for asphalt shingles shall be of a length to penetrate through the roofing materials and a minimum of 3/4 inch (19.1 mm) into the roof sheathing.

question: What minimum number of fasteners are required per asphalt shingle strip?
answer: Asphalt shingles shall be secured to the roof with not less than four fasteners per strip shingle or two fasteners per individual shingle.
ground_truth: Section 1507.2.7: Asphalt shingles shall be secured to the roof with not less than four fasteners per strip shingle or two fasteners per individual shingle.

question: What is the minimum width required for open valley linings when constructed with metal?
answer: For open valleys with metal linings, the valley lining shall be at least 16 inches wide of any corrosion-resistant metals listed in Table 1503.2.
ground_truth: Section 1507.2.9.2: For open valleys (valley lining exposed) lined with metal, the valley lining shall be at least 16 inches (406 mm) wide.

question: What materials must be used for slate shingles in accordance with Chapter 15?
answer: Slate shingles shall comply with ASTM C406 standards for material specifications.
ground_truth: Section 1507.7.5: Slate shingles shall comply with ASTM C406.

question: What is the minimum roof slope for modified bitumen membrane roofs?
answer: Modified bitumen membrane roofs shall have a design slope of not less than one-fourth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2-percent slope) for drainage.
ground_truth: Section 1507.11.1: Modified bitumen membrane roofs shall have a design slope of not less than one-fourth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2-percent slope) for drainage.

question: What is the minimum roof slope required for single-ply membrane roofs?
answer: Single-ply membrane roofs shall have a design slope of not less than one-fourth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2-percent slope) for drainage.
ground_truth: Section 1507.12.1: Single-ply membrane roofs shall have a design slope of not less than one-fourth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2-percent slope) for drainage.

question: What is the minimum roof slope for sprayed polyurethane foam roofing?
answer: Sprayed polyurethane foam roofs shall have a design slope of not less than one-fourth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2-percent slope) for drainage.
ground_truth: Section 1507.14.1: Sprayed polyurethane foam roofs shall have a design slope of not less than one-fourth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2-percent slope) for drainage.

question: What is the minimum roof slope for liquid-applied roofing?
answer: Liquid-applied roofing shall have a design slope of not less than one-fourth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2-percent slope).
ground_truth: Section 1507.15.1: Liquid-applied roofing shall have a design slope of not less than one-fourth unit vertical in 12 units horizontal (2-percent slope).

question: What is the minimum thickness required for sawn lumber used for load-supporting purposes in buildings?
answer: Computations to determine the required sizes of members shall be based on the net dimensions (actual sizes) and not nominal sizes.
ground_truth: Section 2304.2: Computations to determine the required sizes of members shall be based on the net dimensions (actual sizes) and not nominal sizes.

question: What standards must sawn lumber used for load-supporting purposes conform to?
answer: Sawn lumber used for load-supporting purposes shall be identified by the grade mark of a lumber grading or inspection agency approved by an accreditation body that complies with DOC PS 20 or equivalent.
ground_truth: Section 2303.1.1: Sawn lumber used for load-supporting purposes shall be identified by the grade mark of a lumber grading or inspection agency that has been approved by an accreditation body that complies with DOC PS 20 or equivalent.

question: What is the minimum bottom plate thickness required for wall studs in wood frame construction?
answer: Studs shall have full bearing on a 2-inch-thick (actual 1-1/2-inch) or larger plate or sill having a width at least equal to the width of the studs.
ground_truth: Section 2304.3.1: Studs shall have full bearing on a 2-inch-thick (actual 11/2-inch, 38 mm) or larger plate or sill having a width at least equal to the width of the studs.

question: What materials are acceptable for wood structural panels when used structurally?
answer: Wood structural panels when used structurally shall conform to DOC PS 1, DOC PS 2 or ANSI/APA PRP 210 and be identified for grade, bond classification, and Performance Category by an approved testing agency.
ground_truth: Section 2303.1.5: Wood structural panels shall conform to the requirements for their type in DOC PS 1, DOC PS 2 or ANSI/APA PRP 210.

question: What moisture content is required for preservative-treated wood when used in enclosed locations?
answer: Where preservative-treated wood is used in enclosed locations, such wood shall be at a moisture content of 19 percent or less before being covered with insulation or other materials.
ground_truth: Section 2303.1.9.2: Where preservative-treated wood is used in enclosed locations where drying in service cannot readily occur, such wood shall be at a moisture content of 19 percent or less.

question: What is the maximum flame spread index allowed for fire-retardant-treated wood?
answer: Fire-retardant-treated wood shall have a listed flame spread index of 25 or less when tested in accordance with ASTM E84 or UL 723.
ground_truth: Section 2303.2: Fire-retardant-treated wood shall have, when tested in accordance with ASTM E84 or UL 723, a listed flame spread index of 25 or less.

question: What is the minimum pressure required for the pressure process treatment of fire-retardant-treated wood products?
answer: For wood products impregnated with chemicals by a pressure process, the process shall be performed in closed vessels under pressures not less than 50 pounds per square inch gauge (psig).
ground_truth: Section 2303.2.1: For wood products impregnated with chemicals by a pressure process, the process shall be performed in closed vessels under pressures not less than 50 pounds per square inch gauge (psig) (345 kPa).

question: What is the required bearing width for beams and girders supported on masonry walls?
answer: Beams, girders or other concentrated loads shall have a bearing of not less than 3 inches upon solid masonry not less than 4 inches in thickness.
ground_truth: Section 2304.6.3: Beams, girders or other concentrated loads shall have a bearing of not less than 3 inches (76 mm) upon solid masonry not less than 4 inches (102 mm) in thickness.

question: What clearance must be provided around stationary equipment in fire pump and sprinkler riser rooms?
answer: Fire pump and sprinkler riser rooms shall be designed with adequate space for all equipment and sufficient working room around the stationary equipment to allow inspection, service, repair or replacement.
ground_truth: Section 901.8: Fire pump rooms and automatic sprinkler system riser rooms shall be designed with adequate space for all equipment necessary for the installation, with sufficient working room around the stationary equipment.

question: What combustible framing clearance is required from chimneys and fireplaces?
answer: Combustible framing shall be a minimum of 2 inches but shall not be less than the distance specified in Sections 2111 and 2113 from flues, chimneys and fireplaces, and 6 inches away from flue openings.
ground_truth: Section 2304.5: Combustible framing shall be a minimum of 2 inches (51 mm), but shall not be less than the distance specified in Sections 2111 and 2113 from flues, chimneys and fireplaces, and 6 inches (152 mm) away from flue openings.

question: What are the minimum bending yield strengths required for nails used in framing?
answer: Nails used for framing connections shall have minimum bending yield strengths of 80 ksi for larger shank diameters, 90 ksi for medium diameters, and 100 ksi for smaller diameters.
ground_truth: Section 2303.6: Nails used for framing and sheathing connections shall have minimum average bending yield strengths as follows: 80 kips per square inch (ksi), 90 ksi, and 100 ksi for different shank diameters.

question: What moisture content is required for fire-retardant-treated wood before use in buildings?
answer: Fire-retardant-treated wood shall be dried to a moisture content of 19 percent or less for lumber and 15 percent or less for wood structural panels before use.
ground_truth: Section 2303.2.8: Fire-retardant-treated wood shall be dried to a moisture content of 19 percent or less for lumber and 15 percent or less for wood structural panels before use.

question: What information must labels of fire-retardant-treated wood contain?
answer: Labels must include the identification mark of an approved agency, identification of the treating manufacturer, name of fire-retardant treatment, species of wood, flame spread index, method of drying after treatment, and conformance with appropriate standards.
ground_truth: Section 2303.2.4: Each piece of fire-retardant-treated lumber and wood structural panels shall be labeled. The label shall contain the identification mark of an approved agency, identification of the treating manufacturer, and the name of the fire-retardant treatment.

question: What testing requirements apply to artificial decorative vegetation placed in outdoor occupancies?
answer: Artificial decorative vegetation shall meet the flame propagation performance criteria of Test Method 1 or Test Method 2 of NFPA 701, or shall be tested in accordance with NFPA 289 using the 20 kW ignition source with a maximum heat release rate of 100 kW.
ground_truth: Section 809.2: Artificial decorative vegetation shall meet the flame propagation performance criteria of NFPA 701 or shall be tested in accordance with NFPA 289, using the 20 kW ignition source, and shall have a maximum heat release rate of 100 kW.

question: What electrical equipment restrictions apply to artificial decorative vegetation?
answer: The use of unlisted electrical wiring and lighting on artificial decorative vegetation is prohibited, and the use of electrical wiring and lighting on artificial trees constructed entirely of metal is prohibited.
ground_truth: Section 809.3: The use of unlisted electrical wiring and lighting on artificial decorative vegetation shall be prohibited. The use of electrical wiring and lighting on artificial trees constructed entirely of metal shall be prohibited.

question: Where are automatic sprinkler systems required in Group A-1 occupancies?
answer: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided where the fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet, has an occupant load of 300 or more, is located on a floor other than exit discharge, or contains a multitheater complex.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.1.1: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided for fire areas containing Group A-1 occupancies where the fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1115 m2) or has an occupant load of 300 or more.

question: What sprinkler system requirement applies to Group A-2 restaurant and cafeteria occupancies?
answer: A restaurant, cafeteria, or similar dining facility is required to have sprinklers only if it has a fire area occupancy load of 200 patrons or more.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.1.2, Exception: A restaurant, cafeteria, or similar dining facility is required to have sprinklers only if it has a fire area occupancy load of 200 patrons or more.

question: Where must automatic sprinkler systems be provided for Group A-5 occupancies?
answer: For Group A-5 occupancies, automatic sprinkler systems shall be provided in concession stands, retail areas, press boxes and other accessory use areas in excess of 1,000 square feet.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.1.5: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided for Group A-5 occupancies in concession stands, retail areas, press boxes and other accessory use areas in excess of 1,000 square feet (93 m2).

question: What automatic sprinkler system requirement applies to ambulatory care facilities?
answer: An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout the entire floor containing an ambulatory care facility where four or more care recipients are incapable of self-preservation.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.2: An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout the entire floor containing an ambulatory care facility where four or more care recipients are incapable of self-preservation.

question: What sprinkler system requirement applies to Group E educational occupancies?
answer: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all Group E fire areas greater than 12,000 square feet and throughout every portion of educational buildings below the lowest level of exit discharge.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.3: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all Group E fire areas greater than 12,000 square feet (1115 m2) and throughout every portion of educational buildings below the lowest level of exit discharge.

question: What conditions require automatic sprinkler systems in Group F-1 industrial facilities?
answer: Automatic sprinkler systems are required where a Group F-1 fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet, is located more than three stories above grade plane, or the combined area exceeds 24,000 square feet.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.4: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided where a Group F-1 fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1115 m2), is located more than three stories above grade plane, or the combined area exceeds 24,000 square feet.

question: What sprinkler system requirement applies to Group F-1 woodworking operations?
answer: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout Group F-1 fire areas containing woodworking operations in excess of 2,500 square feet that generate finely divided combustible waste.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.4.1: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all Group F-1 occupancy fire areas that contain woodworking operations in excess of 2,500 square feet (232 m2).

question: What automatic sprinkler system is required in Group H high-hazard occupancies?
answer: An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed in Group H occupancies as required, including throughout Group H-5 occupancies and in buildings where pyroxylin plastics are stored in quantities exceeding 100 pounds.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.5: Automatic sprinkler systems shall be provided in high-hazard occupancies as required in Sections 903.2.5.1 through 903.2.5.3.

question: What occupancy hazard classifications apply to Group H-5 occupancies for sprinkler design?
answer: Fabrication areas, service corridors, and storage rooms without dispensing require Ordinary Hazard Group 2; storage rooms with dispensing require Extra Hazard Group 2.
ground_truth: TABLE 903.2.5.2 GROUP H-5 SPRINKLER DESIGN CRITERIA: Fabrication areas - Ordinary Hazard Group 2, Storage rooms with dispensing - Extra Hazard Group 2.

question: What automatic sprinkler system requirement applies to Group I institutional occupancies?
answer: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout buildings with a Group I fire area.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.6: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout buildings with a Group I fire area.

question: What conditions require automatic sprinkler systems in Group M retail occupancies?
answer: Automatic sprinkler systems are required where a Group M fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet, is located more than three stories above grade plane, or the combined area exceeds 24,000 square feet.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.7: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided where a Group M fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1115 m2), is located more than three stories above grade plane, or the combined area exceeds 24,000 square feet.

question: What sprinkler system requirement applies to high-piled or rack storage arrays in Group M?
answer: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided in accordance with the Florida Fire Prevention Code in all buildings of Group M where storage of merchandise is in high-piled or rack storage arrays.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.7.1: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided in accordance with the Florida Fire Prevention Code in all buildings of Group M where storage of merchandise is in high-piled or rack storage arrays.

question: What automatic sprinkler system is required for Group R residential occupancies?
answer: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all buildings with a Group R fire area.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.8: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided throughout all buildings with a Group R fire area.

question: What conditions trigger automatic sprinkler requirements in repair garages?
answer: Sprinklers are required in buildings with two or more stories with fire areas exceeding 10,000 square feet, one-story buildings exceeding 12,000 square feet, or those servicing vehicles in basements.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.9.1: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided in buildings having two or more stories with a fire area containing a repair garage exceeding 10,000 square feet (929 m2).

question: What automatic sprinkler system is required for bulk tire storage?
answer: Buildings where the area for tire storage exceeds 20,000 cubic feet shall be equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.9.2: Buildings where the area for the storage of tires exceeds 20,000 cubic feet (566 m3) shall be equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system.

question: What conditions require automatic sprinkler systems in enclosed parking garages?
answer: Sprinkler systems are required where the fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet or where the garage is located beneath other groups, except beneath Group R-3 occupancies.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.10: An automatic sprinkler system shall be provided where the fire area exceeds 12,000 square feet (1115 m2) or where the enclosed parking garage is located beneath other groups.

question: What sprinkler requirement applies to stories without adequate exterior wall openings?
answer: An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout all stories where the floor area exceeds 1,500 square feet and there is not adequate exterior wall opening.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.11.1: An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed throughout all stories where the floor area exceeds 1,500 square feet (139.4 m2) and there is not adequate exterior wall opening.

question: What automatic sprinkler system requirement applies to rubbish and linen chutes?
answer: An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed at the top of rubbish and linen chutes and in their terminal rooms, with additional heads at alternate floors.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.11.2: An automatic sprinkler system shall be installed at the top of rubbish and linen chutes and in their terminal rooms.

question: What is the automatic sprinkler system requirement for buildings three stories or more in height?
answer: Any building three stories or more in height shall be equipped with an approved automatic sprinkler system.
ground_truth: Section 903.2.11.3: Any building which is of three stories or more in height shall be equipped with an approved automatic sprinkler system.

question: What fire protection system supervision requirement applies in buildings?
answer: Where required, fire protection systems shall be monitored by an approved supervising station in accordance with NFPA 72.
ground_truth: Section 901.6: Where required, fire protection systems shall be monitored by an approved supervising station in accordance with NFPA 72.

question: What testing is required for fire protection systems before occupancy?
answer: Fire protection systems shall be tested and it shall be unlawful to occupy portions of a structure until the required fire protection systems have been tested and approved.
ground_truth: Section 901.5: Fire protection systems shall be tested. It shall be unlawful to occupy portions of a structure until the required fire protection systems within that portion of the structure have been tested and approved.

question: What is required when fire protection systems must be modified or removed in buildings?
answer: Persons shall not remove or modify any fire protection system installed or maintained without approval by the building official.
ground_truth: Section 901.3: Persons shall not remove or modify any fire protection system installed or maintained under the provisions of this code without approval by the building official.

question: What thread type requirement applies to fire department connections for sprinkler systems?
answer: Threads for fire department connections shall be compatible with the connections used by the local fire department.
ground_truth: Section 901.4: Threads provided for fire department connections to sprinkler systems shall be compatible with the connections used by the local fire department.

question: What is the minimum thickness required for the plumbing vent pipe in residential plumbing systems?
answer: Vent pipe sizing and materials must comply with standards for either service or distribution piping, with specific pressure ratings.
ground_truth: Section P2906.4 and P2906.5: Water service and distribution piping materials must meet specified standards with appropriate pressure ratings.

question: What is the maximum length of hot water piping allowed from the source to fixtures in residential plumbing?
answer: The developed length of hot water piping from the source to the fixtures that require hot water shall not exceed 100 feet.
ground_truth: Section P2905.3: The developed length of hot water piping shall not exceed 100 feet.

question: What lead content restrictions apply to water supply pipe and fittings in residential plumbing?
answer: The lead content in pipe and fittings shall not be greater than 8 percent, and for drinking purposes, the weighted average lead content shall be 0.25 percent or less.
ground_truth: Section P2906.2: The lead content in pipe and fittings used in the water supply system shall be not greater than 8 percent. Section P2906.2.1: For drinking water purposes, shall have a weighted average lead content of 0.25 percent lead or less.

question: What minimum separation distance is required between water service and building sewer in residential plumbing?
answer: Where the building sewer does not minimize contamination risk, the water service and building sewer shall be separated by not less than 5 feet of undisturbed or compacted earth.
ground_truth: Section P2906.4.1: The water service pipe and the building sewer shall be horizontally separated by not less than 5 feet (1524 mm) of undisturbed or compacted earth.

question: What materials are permitted for water distribution pipe in residential dwellings?
answer: Water-distribution piping shall conform to NSF 61 and Table P2906.5, including copper, CPVC, PEX, PEX-AL-PEX, galvanized steel, and other approved materials.
ground_truth: Section P2906.5: Water-distribution piping shall conform to NSF 61 and one of the standards indicated in Table P2906.5.

question: What are the requirements for polyethylene plastic pipe joints in residential plumbing?
answer: Joints between polyethylene plastic pipe and fittings shall be made by solvent cementing, heat fusion, corrosion-resistant metal clamps, or compression connections.
ground_truth: Section P2906.9: Joints in plastic piping shall be made by solvent cementing, heat fusion, corrosion-resistant metal clamps with insert fittings or compression connections.

question: What is the minimum water pressure rating required for water distribution pipe in residential plumbing?
answer: Water-distribution pipe and tubing shall have a pressure rating of not less than 100 psi at 180°F.
ground_truth: Section P2906.5: Water-distribution pipe and tubing shall have a pressure rating of not less than 100 psi at 180°F (689 kPa at 82°C).

question: What testing standards apply to drinking water treatment units in residential plumbing?
answer: Drinking water treatment units shall meet the requirements of NSF 42, NSF 44, NSF 53, NSF 62, or CSA B483.1.
ground_truth: Section P2909.1: Drinking water treatment units shall meet the requirements of NSF42, NSF 44, NSF 53, NSF 62 or CSA B483.1.

question: What scope governs nonpotable water systems in residential applications per Chapter P2910?
answer: Nonpotable water systems shall comply with provisions governing materials, design, construction and installation, and use must comply with applicable laws, rules and ordinances.
ground_truth: Section P2910.1: The provisions of this section shall govern the materials, design, construction and installation of systems for the collection, storage, treatment and distribution of nonpotable water.

question: What is the minimum nominal thickness of masonry bearing walls more than one story high?
answer: The minimum thickness of masonry bearing walls more than one story high shall be 8 inches.
ground_truth: Section R606.4.1: The minimum thickness of masonry bearing walls more than one story high shall be 8 inches (203 mm).

question: What is the maximum corbeled projection allowed for multiwythe masonry walls bonded by mortar or grout?
answer: The maximum corbeled projection beyond the face of the wall for multiwythe walls bonded by mortar or grout shall not exceed one-half of the wall thickness.
ground_truth: Section R606.5.2: The maximum corbeled projection beyond the face of the wall shall not exceed one-half of the wall thickness for multiwythe walls bonded by mortar or grout.

question: What is the minimum bearing length required for joists supported on masonry walls?
answer: Joists shall have a bearing of not less than 1-1/2 inches and shall be supported in accordance with Section R606.1.
ground_truth: Section R606.6.3.1: Joists shall have a bearing of not less than 11/2 inches (38 mm).

question: What is the minimum mortar joint coverage required for wall ties from the exposed face in residential masonry?
answer: Wall ties shall have not less than 5/8-inch mortar coverage from the exposed face.
ground_truth: Section R606.3.3: Wall ties shall have not less than 5/8-inch (15.9 mm) mortar coverage from the exposed face.

question: What is the maximum height allowed for unreinforced solid masonry parapet walls?
answer: Unreinforced solid masonry parapet walls shall be not less than 8 inches thick and their height shall not exceed four times their thickness.
ground_truth: Section R606.4.4: Unreinforced solid masonry parapet walls shall not exceed four times their thickness.

question: What is the maximum height allowed for unreinforced hollow unit masonry parapet walls?
answer: Unreinforced hollow unit masonry parapet walls shall be not less than 8 inches thick and their height shall not exceed three times their thickness.
ground_truth: Section R606.4.4: Unreinforced hollow unit masonry parapet walls shall not exceed three times their thickness.

question: What minimum corrosion protection is required for joint reinforcement in interior masonry walls?
answer: Joint reinforcement for interior walls shall conform to ASTM A641, Class 1 minimum corrosion protection.
ground_truth: TABLE R606.3.4.1: Joint reinforcement, interior walls - ASTM A641, Class 1

question: What minimum coverage is required for bar reinforcement exposed to weather or soil?
answer: Where reinforcement is exposed to weather or soil, the minimum coverage shall be 2 inches.
ground_truth: Section R606.3.4: For weather or soil exposure, minimum coverage shall be 2 inches (51 mm).

question: What is the maximum fine grout pour height for grouted masonry construction?
answer: Fine grout has a maximum pour height of 1 foot with minimum grout space width of 0.75 inches.
ground_truth: TABLE R606.3.5.1: Fine grout - 1 foot maximum pour height, 0.75 inch minimum width of grout spaces.

question: What is the maximum coarse grout pour height for grouted masonry construction?
answer: Coarse grout has a maximum pour height of 1 foot with minimum grout space width of 1.5 inches.
ground_truth: TABLE R606.3.5.1: Coarse grout - 1 foot maximum pour height, 1.5 inch minimum width of grout spaces.

question: What is the spacing requirement for vertical reinforcement in grouted masonry construction?
answer: Vertical reinforcement shall be held at top and bottom and at intervals not exceeding 200 diameters of the reinforcement.
ground_truth: Section R606.3.5.3: Vertical reinforcement shall be held at intervals not exceeding 200 diameters of the reinforcement.

question: What is the maximum head joint offset required for masonry laid in running bond?
answer: Head joints in successive courses shall be offset by not less than one-fourth the unit length.
ground_truth: Section R606.3.7.1: Head joints in successive courses shall be offset by not less than one-fourth the unit length.

question: What minimum area of horizontal reinforcement is required for masonry laid in stack bond?
answer: The minimum area of horizontal reinforcement in bed joints spaced not more than 48 inches apart shall be 0.0007 times the vertical cross-sectional area of the wall.
ground_truth: Section R606.3.7.2: The minimum area of horizontal reinforcement shall be 0.0007 times the vertical cross-sectional area of the wall.

question: What is the minimum bearing area requirement for concrete block or masonry walls supporting loads?
answer: Each masonry wythe shall be supported by at least two-thirds of the wythe thickness.
ground_truth: Section R606.6.1: Each masonry wythe shall be supported by at least two-thirds of the wythe thickness.

question: What minimum bearing is required for beams and girders supported on masonry walls?
answer: Beams, girders or other concentrated loads shall have a bearing of not less than 3 inches upon solid masonry not less than 4 inches in thickness.
ground_truth: Section R606.6.3: Beams shall have a bearing of not less than 3 inches (76 mm) upon solid masonry not less than 4 inches (102 mm) in thickness.

question: What maximum chase depth is allowed in masonry walls?
answer: Chases and recesses in masonry walls shall not be deeper than one-third the wall thickness, with maximum horizontal length of 4 feet.
ground_truth: Section R606.8: Chases and recesses shall not be deeper than one-third the wall thickness, and the maximum length shall not exceed 4 feet (1219 mm).

question: What minimum masonry is required behind chases and recesses in residential walls?
answer: Chases and recesses shall have not less than 8 inches of masonry in back of the chases and between adjacent openings.
ground_truth: Section R606.8: Shall have not less than 8 inches (203 mm) of masonry in back of the chases and recesses.

question: What maximum height-to-thickness ratio is permitted for masonry piers?
answer: The unsupported height of masonry piers shall not exceed 10 times their least dimension.
ground_truth: Section R606.7: The unsupported height of masonry piers shall not exceed 10 times their least dimension.

question: What requirements apply to filled hollow piers in masonry construction?
answer: Hollow piers shall be capped with 4 inches of solid masonry, a masonry cap block, or have cavities of the top course filled with concrete or grout.
ground_truth: Section R606.7.1: Hollow piers shall be capped with 4 inches (102 mm) of solid masonry or concrete, a masonry cap block, or have cavities filled.

question: What minimum compression strength allows for allowable compressive stresses of 160 psi for solid masonry?
answer: Solid masonry of brick with compressive strength of 2,500 psi allows allowable compressive stresses of 160 psi with Type M or S mortar.
ground_truth: TABLE R606.9: Solid masonry - 2,500 psi - 160 psi (Type M or S mortar)

question: What minimum thickness of solid masonry is required for bearing under concentrated loads?
answer: Beams, girders or other concentrated loads shall be supported upon solid masonry not less than 4 inches in thickness.
ground_truth: Section R606.6.3: Beams shall have a bearing upon solid masonry not less than 4 inches (102 mm) in thickness.

question: What provisions must be made for mortar between masonry units and reinforcement?
answer: The thickness of grout or mortar between masonry units and reinforcement shall not be less than 1/4 inch.
ground_truth: Section R606.3.5.3: The thickness of grout or mortar shall not be less than 1/4 inch (6.4 mm).

question: What masonry materials are allowed to be used for corbeling in residential construction?
answer: Solid masonry units or masonry units filled with mortar or grout shall be used for corbeling.
ground_truth: Section R606.5.1: Solid masonry units or masonry units filled with mortar or grout shall be used for corbeling.

question: What is the maximum projection of one corbeling unit in masonry?
answer: The maximum projection of one unit shall not exceed one-half the height of the unit or one-third the thickness at right angles to the wall.
ground_truth: Section R606.5.2: The maximum projection of one unit shall not exceed one-half the height of the unit or one-third the thickness.

question: What wall tie embedment depth is required in solid masonry units?
answer: Wall ties shall be embedded in mortar bed not less than 1-1/2 inches for solid masonry units or solid grouted units.
ground_truth: Section R606.3.3: For solid masonry units, wall ties shall be embedded in mortar bed not less than 11/2 inches (38 mm).

question: What is the required solid masonry unit placement requirement in residential construction?
answer: Solid masonry units shall be laid with full head and bed joints and all interior vertical joints that are designed to receive mortar shall be filled.
ground_truth: Section R606.3.2.1: Solid masonry units shall be laid with full head and bed joints and all interior vertical joints that are designed to receive mortar shall be filled.

question: What joint reinforcement minimum thickness is required in masonry construction?
answer: Joint reinforcement embedded in horizontal mortar joints shall have not less than 5/8-inch mortar coverage from the exposed face.
ground_truth: Section R606.3.4: Joint reinforcement embedded in horizontal mortar joints shall not have less than 5/8-inch (15.9 mm) mortar coverage from the exposed face.

question: What is the minimum bearing length requirement for beam supports on masonry in residential construction?
answer: Beams and girders shall have a minimum bearing length of 3 inches measured parallel to the beam.
ground_truth: Section R606.6.3: Beams shall have a bearing of not less than 3 inches (76 mm) in length measured parallel to the beam.

question: What sizing and design standards apply to prefabricated wood I-joists in residential framing?
answer: Structural capacities and design provisions for prefabricated wood I-joists shall be established and monitored in accordance with ASTM D5055.
ground_truth: Section 2303.1.2: Structural capacities and design provisions for prefabricated wood I-joists shall be established and monitored in accordance with ASTM D5055.

question: What scope governs the provisions of Chapter 9 fire protection systems?
answer: The provisions of Chapter 9 shall specify where fire protection systems are required and shall apply to the design, installation and operation of fire protection systems and carbon monoxide detection alarms.
ground_truth: Section 901.1: The provisions of this chapter shall specify where fire protection systems are required and shall apply to the design, installation and operation of fire protection systems and carbon monoxide detection alarms.

question: What alternative fire protection systems may be provided instead of automatic sprinklers?
answer: Alternative automatic fire-extinguishing systems complying with Section 904 shall be permitted instead of automatic sprinkler protection where recognized by the applicable standard and approved by the fire code official.
ground_truth: Section 903.1.1: Alternative automatic fire-extinguishing systems complying with Section 904 shall be permitted instead of automatic sprinkler protection where recognized by the applicable standard and approved by the fire code official.

question: What radon concentration level is equivalent to the Florida Department of Health exposure standard of 0.02 working levels under typical home conditions?
answer: The Florida Department of Health exposure standard is equivalent to an annual average radon level of 4.0 picocuries per liter (pCi/l) under conditions often encountered in homes.
ground_truth: Section C103: The Department of Health (DOH) has set an exposure standard for radon decay products in buildings at an annual average of 0.02 working levels. Under conditions often encountered in homes, this is equivalent to an annual average radon level of 4.0 picocuries per liter.

question: Must a post-mitigation indoor radon concentration test be conducted to demonstrate successful radon mitigation?
answer: Yes, a post-mitigation indoor radon concentration test must be conducted to demonstrate successful mitigation in compliance with the rules of the Department of Health and Chapter 3 of the standard.
ground_truth: Section C101.2: A post-mitigation indoor radon concentration test must be conducted to demonstrate successful mitigation in compliance with the rules of the Department of Health and Chapter 3 of this standard.

question: Does the Florida Building Code apply to detached one- and two-family dwellings up to three stories above grade plane?
answer: No. Detached one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses not more than three stories above grade plane shall comply with the Florida Building Code, Residential instead.
ground_truth: Section 101.2 Exception 1: Detached one- and two-family dwellings and multiple single-family dwellings (townhouses) not more than three stories above grade plane in height with a separate means of egress shall comply with the Florida Building Code, Residential.

question: Which building code requirements are not utilized or enforced in Florida?
answer: Code requirements that address snow loads and earthquake protection are not utilized or enforced in Florida.
ground_truth: Section 101.2 Exception 2: Code requirements that address snow loads and earthquake protection shall not be utilized or enforced.

question: When is an approved research report required to support the use of a product or material not specifically provided for in the Florida Building Code?
answer: An approved research report is required when sufficient technical data is needed to substantiate the proposed use of any product, material, or assembly to demonstrate performance for the use intended.
ground_truth: Section 104.11: Sufficient technical data shall be submitted to the building official to substantiate the proposed use of any product, material or assembly.

question: Who bears the cost of tests, reports, and investigations required to approve alternative materials or methods of construction?
answer: The owner or the owner's authorized agent bears the cost of all tests, reports, and investigations required for approval of alternative materials and methods.
ground_truth: Section 104.11: The costs, reports and investigations required under these provisions shall be paid by the owner or the owner's authorized agent.

question: What must an approved agency have to perform required tests for special inspections?
answer: An approved agency must have adequate equipment to perform required tests, and that equipment must be periodically calibrated.
ground_truth: Section 1703.1.2: An approved agency shall have adequate equipment to perform required tests. The equipment shall be periodically calibrated.

question: What permanent information must be included on an exterior window or door label when tested to AAMA/WDMA/CSA standards?
answer: The label must include manufacturer identification, product model/series number, positive and negative design pressure rating, product maximum size tested, impact-resistant rating if applicable, Florida or Miami-Dade approval number, applicable test standards, and the certification agency.
ground_truth: Section 1709.5.1: Information identifying the manufacturer, the product model/series number, positive and negative design pressure rating, product maximum size tested, impact-resistant rating if applicable, Florida product approval number or Miami-Dade product approval number, applicable test standard(s), and approved product certification agency shall be on the label.

question: When is a soils investigation required for a building site?
answer: A soils investigation is required for all building sites except for simple, light-frame structures less than two stories tall built on undisturbed natural soil with favorable characteristics.
ground_truth: Section 1803.2: The owner shall employ a registered design professional for a site-specific geotechnical investigation.

question: What is the minimum depth for foundation footings below the frost line in Florida?
answer: Foundation footings must extend below the frost line depth specified by the local building official, typically a minimum depth below grade.
ground_truth: Section 1804.2: All foundations shall be placed below the frost line.

question: What must be provided when ground water is present at a proposed foundation location?
answer: A site-specific drainage plan must be developed that will prevent water infiltration, maintain bearing capacity, and prevent settlement or heave.
ground_truth: Section 1805.1: Where the investigation indicates ground water within 5 feet of the lowest level of the building, foundation design shall include a statement of protection measures.

question: When is a geotechnical investigation report required to be prepared by a registered design professional?
answer: A geotechnical investigation report is required for all buildings except for simple structures less than two stories, light-frame construction on undisturbed natural soil in favorable locations.
ground_truth: Section 1803.2.1.1: The geotechnical investigation report shall be prepared by a registered design professional.

question: What is required to establish the bearing capacity of soil for building foundations?
answer: Site investigation by a registered design professional must determine actual soil properties through borings, sampling, and testing to establish safe bearing capacity.
ground_truth: Section 1806: Foundation design shall be based on the nature of the soil and the requirements of this chapter.

question: Under what conditions must a perimeter drain system be installed for buildings?
answer: A perimeter drain system must be installed when ground water is present at a depth less than 3 feet below the foundation and the site will not accommodate gravity drainage.
ground_truth: Section 1805.2.1: Where ground water is present, a perimeter drain system shall be installed.

question: What is required for concrete slabs-on-grade in areas with moisture or poor drainage?
answer: A vapor retarder must be installed beneath the slab, and the subgrade must be properly graded and drained to prevent water accumulation.
ground_truth: Section 1904.2: All concrete slabs shall be graded to drain clear of the structure on all sides. Ground slabs shall have an approved under-slab fill or vapor retarder.

question: How deep must foundation footings extend in areas subject to erosion or scour?
answer: Foundation footings in areas prone to erosion or scour must extend below the anticipated scour depth and be protected from erosion by suitable fill or riprap.
ground_truth: Section 1808.1: Where erosion or scour is a concern, foundations shall be designed and constructed below the estimated scour depth.

question: What are the three main components of a water-resistive barrier in exterior wall construction?
answer: The three main components are: (1) a weather-resistant material barrier, (2) a drainage plane to direct water down and out, and (3) flashing at transitions and openings to prevent water entry.
ground_truth: Section 2203.1: All exterior walls shall have a weather-resistant exterior covering and a water-resistive barrier with proper drainage plane and flashing.

question: Is wood sheathing permitted on exterior walls in Florida, and if so, under what conditions?
answer: Yes, wood sheathing is permitted but must comply with specific requirements regarding grade, fastening, and moisture protection according to Chapter 22.
ground_truth: Section 2304: Wood-based products used as exterior wall sheathing shall comply with the requirements of Chapter 23.

question: What flashing requirements apply to windows, doors, and other openings in exterior walls?
answer: Flashing must be installed at all openings to direct water down and out, with flashing extending beneath the water-resistive barrier and over exterior trim, sloped to shed water.
ground_truth: Section 2203.2: Flashing shall be installed to direct water down and out of the wall. Flashing shall extend beneath the water-resistive barrier.

question: What is the maximum allowable use of plastic materials in building construction according to the Florida Building Code?
answer: Plastic materials are limited in use and must comply with specific requirements for flame spread, smoke development, and structural performance based on the material type and application.
ground_truth: Section 2602: Plastics shall only be used where specifically permitted elsewhere in this code.

question: What fire rating is required for foam plastic insulation used in concealed spaces?
answer: Foam plastic insulation must have a flame spread rating of 25 or less and smoke development of 450 or less, or meet alternative fire protection requirements.
ground_truth: Section 2603.2: Foam plastic insulation shall have a flame spread rating not exceeding 25 and a smoke development rating not exceeding 450.

question: When is a thermal barrier required for foam plastic insulation?
answer: A thermal barrier is required on the interior side of foam plastic insulation to protect it from ignition and to provide time for occupant escape.
ground_truth: Section 2603.4: Foam plastic insulation shall be protected by a thermal barrier of 1/2 inch gypsum wallboard or equivalent.

question: Are plastic materials permitted for primary structural elements in buildings?
answer: Plastic materials are generally not permitted as primary structural elements but may be used for specific applications where approved and properly tested.
ground_truth: Section 2602: Plastics shall only be used where specifically permitted and in accordance with the limitations of this chapter.

question: What are the typical requirements for vault dimensions and light wells in public right-of-way encroachments?
answer: Vaults and light wells must meet minimum width, length, and depth requirements established by the building official and must be structurally designed to support overlying loads.
ground_truth: Section 3206: Vaults shall be designed with adequate dimensions and structural capacity to support imposed loads.

question: Is an encroachment permit required for structures extending into public right-of-way such as light wells or storefronts?
answer: Yes, an encroachment permit from the jurisdiction is required for any structure or element that extends into public right-of-way.
ground_truth: Section 3201: Encroachments into public right-of-way shall be authorized by permit.

question: What safety requirements apply to grade-level encroachments such as subway vaults or light wells?
answer: Grade-level encroachments must have protective grating or covers that can safely support pedestrian and vehicular loads and provide adequate drainage.
ground_truth: Section 3209: Subsurface vaults and other grade-level encroachments shall have protective coverings designed to support expected loads.

question: What is required to protect adjacent buildings and property during construction?
answer: Protective measures must be implemented to prevent damage to adjacent structures, utilities, and property, including temporary shoring, bracing, and support systems.
ground_truth: Section 3301: During construction, proper safeguards shall be maintained to protect buildings, structures, utilities and property.

question: When is temporary support of adjacent structures required during construction?
answer: Temporary support is required whenever excavation, demolition, or construction activities could cause movement or damage to adjacent buildings or structures.
ground_truth: Section 3302: Where excavation or construction activities are adjacent to existing structures, temporary support and bracing shall be designed and installed.

question: What is the maximum allowable height for a Group R-3 residential building in Florida?
answer: Group R-3 residential buildings are permitted up to the height limits specified in Table 503 based on construction type and with appropriate setbacks.
ground_truth: Section 503: Buildings shall be limited in height by the type of construction and occupancy classification.

question: How does construction type affect the allowable building height and area?
answer: Higher construction types (I, II) allow greater heights and areas than lower construction types (IV, V). Type I provides the least restrictions while Type V-N provides the most stringent limitations.
ground_truth: Section 503 and Table 503: Building heights and floor areas shall be regulated by type of construction.

question: What frontage increase modifications are permitted for buildings with greater street frontage?
